name: Pier 27
summary_en: Pier 27 has been rebuilt around whatever the waterfront needed at the time. The Port's own 1980 handbook lists Piers 27-29 as a breakbulk terminal — three berths, fifteen acres, 335,830 square feet of covered storage, worked by the Pacific-Oriental Terminal Company and serving Argentine, Philippine and Dutch lines. By the time of the Waterfront Land Use Plan those cargo activities had been consolidated at Pier 80, the piers were designated a transitional maritime area, and the sites were being used for interim non-trust purposes. What replaced the cargo was an event and cruise complex: the Port Commission tracked the Pier 27 cruise terminal for use during the 34th America's Cup, approved revenue bonds for a second phase of the James R. Herman Cruise Terminal, and considered a donor recognition programme at Piers 27/29. The environmental report for that combined project deals in the detail such a shift produces — noise monitoring on Telegraph Hill about 750 feet from the Pier 27 waterfront, and a mitigation measure requiring acoustical enclosures for generators at the Pier 27-29 spectator areas. The contracts recorded against the pier by name are for its public art.

Herman Cruise Terminal and Pier 35 Activity for the period of September 2014 to June 2015 DIRECTOR'S RECOMMENDATION: Informational Only Executive Summary The James R. Herman Cruise Terminal at Pier 27 welcomed its first cruise vessel, Crown Princess, on September 18, 2014. Since then, the Port has received 64 additional ship calls with approximately 227,000 embarking and disembarking passengers. On non-cruise days, the terminal has been utilized for civic and corporate events, including several from San Francisco’s growing technology sector. The facility has hosted 26 special events with one of the first being the San Francisco Giants’ celebration of their participation in the 2014 World Series. This represents a very strong start.
